And in the year 455
of the Arabs (A.D. 1063), Khatun, the wife of Sultan Tughril Beg, died,
she who was very beloved by him,
and by whose hands all royal affairs were managed.
And he sent to the Caliph that he might betroth to him his daughter.
And when the Caliph did not consent that a daughter of theirs should belong to a stranger outside their family and their tribe,
the Sultan took offense.
And after many reproaches,
he even began to show open enmity.
Then the Caliph was afraid,
and unwillingly
he gave him his daughter,
on the condition that she should not depart from the palace,
but whenever the Sultan came to Baghdad,
he would be with her inside the palace.
And after long negotiation it was settled
that she should go out to the new court which the Sultan had built.
And the Sultan came to Baghdad,
and he offered one hundred thousand gold dinars,
and one hundred and fifty thousand silver coins,
and four thousand chief suits of garments;
and he took the daughter of al-Qadir (al-Qa'im?) the Caliph in marriage.
It is said
that when she entered his court,
the Sultan and the Turkish nobles stood up and danced according to their custom,
bending their knees, rising, and singing in Turkish.
And a golden throne was set up for her.
And the Sultan entered, bowed down to the ground, and paid homage to her,
and he did not sit down,
but withdrew and went out.
He did thus for seven days,
without her uncovering her face that he might see it.
And in this wedding there was great joy for the Sultan,
but very great grief for the Caliph;
especially because when the Sultan departed from Baghdad to go to Khorasan,
he took the Caliph's daughter, his wife, with him by force,
and did not keep the condition
that she should not depart from Baghdad.
And in this year, which is the year 1374
of the Greeks (A.D. 1063),
an army of the Romans went out,
and they assaulted the city of Amid for many days.
And when the armies of the Turks and the Arabs gathered against them,
and many were killed on both sides,
they abandoned it and departed.
And on the seventh of Elul (September) of this year,
Sultan Tughril died.
